properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 23 at 12:32AM MDT until September 23 at 2:00AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central El Paso County in western Texas...

* Until 200 AM MDT.

* At 1232 AM MDT, A thunderstorm with torrential rainfall rates has
produced nearly .75 inches of rain in 30 minutes near Socorro. This
storm is about to move over areas in southeast and central El Paso
which have already received up to 1.50 inches of rain earlier this
evening.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of arroyos, urban areas, highways, streets
and underpasses as well as other poor drainage and
low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
East, Central and Southeast El Paso, Mission Valley, Fort Bliss,
Socorro and Sparks.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Ohio...

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Hocking River at Athens.

* WHEN...Until this morning.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Low areas, campground, and private camps
along the river between Athens and Coolville begin to flood. Much
of the city of Athens is protected up to 26 feet by levees. In
Nelsonville, the baseball field adjacent to Lake Hope Drive floods.

- At 1:15 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 20.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 16.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:15 AM EDT Wednesday was 20.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
this morning and continue falling to 9.7 feet early Sunday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 20.1
feet on 02/10/2019.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

The next statement will be issued this morning at 1015 AM EDT.

properties.description:

The National Weather Service in Wakefield has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Cumberland County in central Virginia...
Powhatan County in central Virginia...

* Until 400 AM EDT.

was falling across the warned area. There have been reports of up
to 5.5 inches of rain since 10 PM across western Powhatan County.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Powhatan, Cumberland, Tobaccoville, Ballsville, Sunnyside,
Trenholm, Macon, Guinea Mills, Clinton, Hatchers, Belona, Oak
Forest, Ashby, Whiteville, Grays Siding, Lake Powhatan, Tamworth,
Provost and Rock Castle.

dangers of flooding.

Wakefield Facebook page, or using X @NWSWAKEFIELDVA.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 22 at 11:46PM MDT until September 23 at 1:45AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
At 1146 PM MDT, Thunderstorms have diminished in intensity over the
Otero Mesa. Radar estimates 2.50 to 3 inches of rain fell in Otero
County, northwest of Dell City. This will result in flooding in
various draws that flow towards Dell City. Retention dams will
prevent water from reaching Dell City, but flooding will impact rural
roads north and northwest of town, especially across the New Mexico
border.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rural areas on the Otero Mesa northwest of Dell City.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 9:54PM MDT until September 24 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is likely.

* WHERE...South-central New Mexico.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings
may be flooded. Flood structures, like levees and dams, may be
tested.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A late season plume of deep tropical moisture is transported
northward ahead of an upper-level disturbance, bringing several
rounds of thunderstorms with high rainfall rates to the region
through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms will result in
scattered to numerous instances of flash flooding with some
considerable cases. Wednesday morning is the most likely time to
see excessive rainfall. Rainfall amounts around 2 inches are
likely with isolated amounts of 4 inches or more.
- Central Dona Ana County through southeastern Sierra County are
most likely to see the heaviest rainfall through Wednesday
morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

approach the coast of the Yukon Delta. While the most likely

southern portion of the Yukon Delta coast could see water levels
rise to around 1 to 3 feet above the mean high water line, with
rises more likely to be on the lower side of that range. We will
continue to monitor this system closely.

highest tide line. Southeast winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts up to

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

levels for the Kuskokwim Delta Thursday morning through Saturday

Thursday afternoon will diminish early Friday until the low
pressure system moves west of the coast by Friday afternoon.

50 mph by Friday afternoon. Winds gradually weaken but remain
southerly through Saturday.

normal highest tide line on Thursday, coinciding with the passage
of a frontal system. Water levels could reach up to 4 feet in a
worst case scenario.

For Kipnuk, the highest water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the
normal highest tide line are expected on Friday as a low pressure
system moves west of the coast and winds become southerly. Water
levels could reach 2 to 3 feet in a worst case scenario.

please reference maps.dggs.alaska.gov/akfit/

through Thursday evening.

properties.areaDesc: Interior Kuskokwim Delta
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 12:43PM AKDT until September 26 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Interior Kuskokwim Delta, including Kwethluk, Kasigluk,
Bethel, Napaskiak, Napakiak, Oscarville, and other nearby villages.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rain in combination of persistent high water
levels and storm surge may result in flooding of rivers, creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and
streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Area creeks and streams are running high and could flood
with more heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A strong storm projected to move into the eastern Bering Sea will
bring heavy rainfall and storm surge to the area. The Kuskokwim
River is currently running high, with statistics showing the
river is already above the 90th percentile in flow for this time
of year. 1 to 2 inches of rainfall across the Kilbuck Mountains,
as well as across the lower Kuskokwim, is likely to exacerbate
high water levels for the Kwethluk River, Johnson River / tundra
villages, as well as other smaller tributaries and sloughs of the
Kuskokwim.

Confidence is moderate-to-high that flooding of low-lying areas
will occur for Kwethluk and Kasigluk, where high-water was
reported last week. Confidence is lower for flooding elsewhere
and will be dependent on the rainfall amount and degree of
compounding effects from coastal surge and tide cycle.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

Wednesday with widespread heavy rain.  Scattered occurrences of

likely rain amount by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 1.5 inches many

inch in many locations westward to around Dulce, Gallup, and

succession over some locations, with locally heavier rain amounts
reaching over 4 inches over portions of southern, central, and
eastern New Mexico.  Heavy rain will likely continue Wednesday
night over north-central and eastern New Mexico, then showers and
storms with locally heavy rainfall are forecast to return to much
of the state again on Thursday.

terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams.  As the event
unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone
to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of
storms.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 4:48PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern will continue across western Micronesia
with satellite imagery continuing to show areas of heavy showers and
thunderstorms. Latest satellite-dervied surface wind data depicts 15
to 20 mph west to southwest winds across western Yap State and Palau
with pockets of locally higher winds.

Weather models point to a continuation of these conditions with
periods of locally heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts, and choppy seas. Both
Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of Invest 91W, located near
13N142E, northeast of Yap. 91W is now the subject of a Tropical
Cyclone Formation Alert from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center and
showers are expected to remain mostly numerous to widespread and
heavy at times. Model guidance suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain per day
will be possible through Wednesday, especially for Yap.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next couple of days.
Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.
